result.title: Drop the Details, Get the Gist: Dynamic Conceptual Representation for Video Recognition
result.comment: 25 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables. Accepted to the MM4SciReal Workshop at ACCV 2026
result.summary: Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs), which route predictions through a layer of human-interpretable concepts, have substantially improved the interpretability of visual classification by exposing an explicit, language-based rationale for each prediction. Most existing work focuses on static images, and temporal dynamics in videos have been underexplored in conceptual representation. We propose a framework that extends concept-based image recognition to procedural video understanding. It represents a multi-step video as a temporal sequence of segment-level concept score vectors and feeds this sequence into a Transformer encoder to predict the class label. We also explore a way to estimate the contribution of each concept for further interpretability. We evaluated three concept sets of different granularities on cooking and household-activity videos and found that coarser-grained concepts are sufficient for classifying these videos, which implies that fine-grained textual descriptions may be unnecessary.

AI.brief_summary: 将 concept bottleneck 思路从静态图像扩展到程序性视频：把多步视频表示为分段概念得分向量序列，经 Transformer 编码后预测类别，并估计各概念对预测的贡献；在烹饪与家务视频上比较三种粒度概念集，发现粗粒度概念已足够。
AI.relevance_reason: 分段概念得分序列是一种显式中间状态，其「粗粒度概念即可判别」的结论可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节是否必要与信息坍缩问题；概念贡献估计或可为 latent 内容的贡献分配提供线索，但论文不涉及生成式推理。
